plan: This is a second-price auction (I pay the second-highest bid if I win). In such auctions, the dominant strategy is to bid exactly my true value. Bidding higher risks paying more than the item is worth if I win against a bid between my value and my bid. Bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. Since my value is $9, I will bid exactly $9 to ensure I only win when profitable and pay a fair price determined by the second-highest bid.

This is a second-price auction where bidding my true value is the dominant strategy. If I win, I pay the second-highest bid, not my own bid, so there's no benefit to shading my bid up or down. My value is $9, so I'll bid exactly that. If I win, I pay less than $9 (whatever the second-highest bid is), guaranteeing non-negative profit. If I lose, I pay nothing and lose nothing.

This is a second-price auction, where bidding your true value is the dominant strategy. Bidding exactly my value ensures I never overpay (I only pay the second-highest bid if I win) and I never miss out on profitable wins.
